elements.text: Sudden onset of generalised itch/rash, face/tongue itch/swelling, tight throat, hoarseness, cough, difficulty breathing, wheeze, chest pain, dizziness/collapse, abdominal pain/ nausea/vomiting/diarrhoea or exposure to possible allergen3, anaphylaxis likely 28

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Manage and refer urgently:

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If bleeding, apply direct pressure and elevate limb.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If shock2 /systolic BP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV rapidly, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Remove loose/dead skin. Wash wound with soap under running water for 15 minutes, clean with chlorhexidine 0.05% or povidone iodine 10% solution. Apply dressing. Avoid suturing wound.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If snake bite or venom in eyes:

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Keep patient calm and still. Immobilise limb and remove jewellery. Avoid applying tourniquet or sucking/squeezing out venom. Discuss with Poisons Information Helpline 200.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If venom in eyes, immediately flush under running water or sodium chloride 0.9% for 20 minutes. If available, instil 1 drop tetracaine 1% eye drops before irrigating.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: If very painful scorpion sting, inject lidocaine 2% 2mL around site and apply ice if tolerated.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently:
elements.text: Give tetanus toxoid 0.5mL IM if none in past 5 years.

1Obtain description of spider/snake/scorpion, to help with specific management once referred. 2If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 3Medications, new food or insect bite/sting within the last few hours. 3Sick animal (weak, drooling, unsteady gait) or domestic animal with unusual aggression or wild animal that appears tame. 4Symptomatic HIV infection, cancer receiving chemotherapy/radiotherapy, dialysis or long-term corticosteroids. 5Inject as much rabies immunoglobulin as bite site allows. If multiple bites, dilute in equal volumes of saline and infiltrate all wounds. Do not exceed maximum dose. 6Previous anaphylaxis/urticaria/angioedema. 7Advise no alcohol until 48 hours after last dose.

Approach to the patient with a bite/sting not needing urgent attention • Wash wound with soap under running water for 15 minutes, then clean with chlorhexidine 0.05% or povidone iodine 10% solution. • If wound anywhere other than head/face, avoid suturing wound. Dress and check wound every 2 days. If bite on hand, discuss with doctor and refer. • Give tetanus toxoid 0.5mL IM if none in past 5 years. If pain, give paracetamol 500mg-1g orally 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. • Manage further according to type of bite or exposure:
Animal bite: was bite from a dog, cat, cow, goat, donkey, horse, sheep, mongoose, jackal, seal or any contact with a bat?

Human bite
• If broken skin, give post- exposure prophylaxis (PEP) 122. • Give antibiotics:
Give amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 875/125mg 12 hourly for 5 days. If severe penicillin allergy6, give instead azithromycin 500mg once daily for
3 days and metronidazole7 400mg 8 hourly for 5 days. If wound infected, continue antibiotics for 10 days. If no better on antibiotics, refer.
